source_claims.text: If the characteristic functions of probability laws P_n converge pointwise to c and c is continuous at zero, then the sequence P_n is tight.
The proof uses Fubini, computes the inner exponential integral, combines them into the averaged sine-kernel identity, and derives the tail probability bound.
Continuity at zero and dominated convergence make the characteristic-function integral small for all sufficiently large n.
The finitely many early measures are absorbed by increasing the cutoff, giving a uniform tail bound and hence Definition 14.3 tightness.
